issue_context.title: Width-defining Dialog titles issue with close button
comments: I find that the function: ```cpp Widget* Widget::pick(const gfx::Point& pt, const bool checkParentsVisibility) const ``` checks the widgets recursively using the following scheme: ```cpp for (Widget* child : m_children) { inside = child->pick(pt, false); if (inside) { picked = inside; break; ``` So, the order of the children matters. The first child is the first widget tested. On custom dialogs the children order is: 1. Title label 2. Close button That's why the reason of the current issue. On the other hand, in built-in dialogs (like the Preferences dialog), the first item in 'm_children' is the Close Button, so the current problem is non-existent, but I see this other UI problem: The children order is used to draw the widget elements too. So the title overlaps the Close button. Possible solution: - Always insert the title label as the first element (to solve the overlap between the Close button and the title). And test the children vector in reverse order (to solve the current issue). I'm thinking of other alternatives.
